legacyRecord.name: bZx sUSD Kyber spot-price manipulation
legacyRecord.notes: The BZxOracle priced collateral off Kyber's getExpectedRate; the attacker bought sUSD from the Synthetix depot at ~$1 and then pushed the Kyber sUSD/ETH spot rate above $2 through the Uniswap and Synthetix reserves, so the oracle returned a doubled sUSD value and the protocol lent 6,796 ETH against it - the contracts behaved exactly as written, only the consumed price was wrong.

sources.ref: onchain review: the transaction goes attacker EOA 0xb8c6ad5fe7cb6cc72f2c4196dca11fbb272a8cbf -> iETH LoanToken 0x77f973fcaf871459aa58cd81881ce453759281bc flashBorrowToken (0x66fa576f) -> attacker contract 0x360f85f0b74326cddff33a812b05353bc537747b, which round-trips sUSD through the Synthetix depot 0x172e09691dfbbc035e37c73b62095caa16ee2388 and 19 Kyber trades before borrowing; the price the borrow is sized against is read by BZxOracle 0xaa6198fe597dfc331471ae7deba026fb299297fc, which STATICCALLs Kyber 0x818e6fecd516ecc3849daf6845e3ec868087b755 getExpectedRate (0x809a9e55) six times. That oracle was created 2020-02-17T00:55:43Z (block 9498957) by 0xadff3ada12ed0f8a87e31e5a04dfd2ee054e1118, the bZx deployer, unrelated to the attack sender - it is the replacement oracle bZx shipped after the 2020-02-15 incident, in use for 20.97 hours before this one. It is a plain non-proxy contract: no DELEGATECALL appears in the exploit trace and its codehash is identical (0xdb972a7db9bbcc6b4131490943344fac3aaa3e67836e7553135861350e2bc869) at its creation block and at the incident block, so the age is measured from deployment. Classified oracle-manipulation, not code-bug: the flaw is in trusting a manipulable Kyber spot rate, not in bZx's own logic. Loss not recorded in USD: attacker contract 0x360f85f0 held 0 ETH before the transaction and 2,378.153715 ETH after, while the iETH pool's WETH balance fell from 18,586.28 to 11,787.02 WETH. Order-of-magnitude sanity check only (ETH ~ $270 in Feb 2020, so ~$0.6m): far above the $1,000 floor.
loss converted at the incident timestamp (1581995638) via DefiLlama coins: 2,378 ETH x $268.14 = $637,640

disposition.reason: An admitted incident declares this discovery lead.

legacyRecord.name: Conic
legacyRecord.notes: Read-only reentrancy on Curve remove_liquidity skews GenericOracle LP prices used by the ETH omnipool.

sources.ref: Recheck of the deployment basis (DELEGATECALL audit): the ETH omnipool is not a proxy (no EIP-1967 implementation or beacon slot) and its own runtime is byte-identical at the creation block 17592111 and the incident block 17740955, but ConicEthPool executes two external handlers by DELEGATECALL - controller.curveHandler() and controller.convexHandler() (Address.functionDelegateCall at ConicEthPool.sol lines 277/290/461/470) - so its executing code can be repointed from the immutable Controller 0x013A3Da6591d3427F164862793ab4e388F9B587e. Binary-searching eth_getStorageAt on the Controller shows curveHandler (slot 6) changed at block 17613432, 2023-07-03T12:26:23Z (timestamp 1688387183), from 0x92bffb71bbe241ba9cdfb3a4e56e48dc4f118ed7 to 0xD775ae26F89bcd89e66485324D8830c0EF1e8B6c, corroborated by the Controller's own CurveHandlerSet(address) log (topic 0x40f17cc99608acc0aa583a98bd741564e79111d55e65adc0399f400a707d4831, data 0x...d775ae26) in tx 0x0b1dfe6ee755dc11a9a0d0823e22abcc0cb1f03e5ed0673c1f68183cf84f58e6, sent by the Conic deployer 0xc0f0c674dcf195e2c39dfa7bb59fa968b7f7c575 through the governance proxy 0xcb7c67bdde9f7af0667e8d82bb87f1432bd1d902 - a protocol action, not the attacker's; convexHandler (slot 7) held 0x635228EDAEAd8a76b6ae1779bd7682043321943D unchanged over the same range, and the new curveHandler 0xD775ae26F89bcd89e66485324D8830c0EF1e8B6c (created block 17591566 by the pool's own deployer 0xedaeb101f34d767f263c0fe6b8d494e3d071f0ba) has no DELEGATECALL and identical code from its install to the incident. The last change to the executing code is therefore the curveHandler swap, not the pool deployment: lastChangeTimestamp 1688387183, codeAgeSeconds 1689935711-1688387183 = 1548528 (17.92 d instead of 20.92 d). For completeness the Controller's priceOracle (slot 8) was also repointed twice in the window, last at block 17634814 (2023-07-06T12:29:35Z) to GenericOracle 0x286eF89cD2DA6728FD2cb3e1d1c5766Bcea344b0 - the feed the read-only reentrancy skews - but that oracle is reached by CALL, not DELEGATECALL, so it is not part of the victim's executing code and is not used as the basis.

sources.ref: onchain review: exploit tx emits Transfer(0x0 -> 0x548c63a6a7299ab54762e1bfa6b56c1b94c2a820, 500000 GNUS) on the token 0x614577036f0a024dbc1c88ba616b394dd65d105a; the tx is signed by the Axelar ITS executor 0xc77820eef59629fc8d88154977bc8de8a1b2f4ae, so the attacker EOA recorded here is the mint recipient that dumped into the pool in 0xe8a5780cc89d9115acf307da9e6fae68e8b3634a8b41c77d81e95edb9085a407. Token created 2024-02-20 by the GNUS deployer 0x1804deca63705e18edf04f242b325bcd54a8b463 (the wallet whose key leaked), not by the attacker; it is a Diamond, so facet changes emit no EIP-1967 Upgraded event and the age may be overstated. Tier-1 measurement: the diamond emits DiamondCut(...) rather than EIP-1967 Upgraded, and eth_getLogs over [creation 19269335, incident 19802980] returns 10 DiamondCut events - block 19269335 (2024-02-20, deployment cut), 19273203/19273274/19273280/19273284/19273286/19273329/19273367/19273421 (all 2024-02-21) and a final one at block 19762552 (2024-04-29T17:47:59Z, tx 0x5d1ca14aa4eb0ce2c6f953fe6f3856bfbecbfb0945ec9a8420fb61d8152d0808) that re-cut the ERC20 and mint/burn facets six days before the exploit, so the age is measured from that cut (5.65 days) instead of deployment (74.8 days).

disposition.reason: The legacy category key-compromise is outside the EVM code-bug cohort.

legacyRecord.name: Harvest Finance fUSDC vault (Curve y pool price manipulation)
legacyRecord.notes: The fUSDC vault priced deposits and withdrawals off the instantaneous share price of the Curve y pool it farmed, so flash-loan swaps that skewed that pool let the attacker mint fUSDC cheaply and redeem it at the restored price; the vault code itself behaved as written.

sources.ref: onchain review: fUSDC vault 0xf0358e8c created 2020-10-19 by 0xf00dd244228f51547f0563e60bca65a30fbf5f7f, not by attack sender 0xf224ab00; the cited tx is one of the ~17 repeated mint/redeem rounds and its logs touch the fUSDC vault (not the fUSDT vault) Recheck of the deployment basis (DELEGATECALL audit): the fUSDC vault is an EIP-1967 proxy; its implementation slot holds 0x9b3be0cc5dd26fd0254088d03d8206792715588b at both the creation block 11086842 and the incident block 11129474, and a binary search of eth_getStorageAt over that range finds no intermediate write (the slot was read directly rather than relying on Upgraded events); the proxy runtime is byte-identical at both blocks and the implementation contains no DELEGATECALL of its own, so the six-and-a-half-day age is measured from the right point.

disposition.reason: An admitted incident declares this discovery lead.

legacyRecord.name: Lodestar plvGLP exchange-rate manipulation
legacyRecord.notes: The lending market behaved as designed; Lodestar's plvGLP oracle derived the collateral price from the GlpDepositor's assets-per-share ratio, and the attacker inflated that ratio with GlpDepositor.donate() so a flash-loaned plvGLP position could borrow out the other Lodestar markets.

sources.ref: onchain review: lplvGLP market 0xcc25dac54a1a62061b596fd3baf7d454f34c56ff created 2022-11-21 by 0x67e57a0ec37768eaf99a364975ec4e1f98920d01 (Lodestar deployer), unrelated to attack sender 0xc29d94386ff784006ff8461c170d1953cc9e2b5c; no EIP-1967 Upgraded events, so the market code was 18.9 days old; reported attacker profit ~$6.5M against ~$6.9M of protocol loss Recheck of the deployment basis (DELEGATECALL audit): the victim is a Compound-fork CErc20Delegator, whose implementation lives in plain storage slot 18 rather than an EIP-1967 slot; binary-searching eth_getStorageAt on slot 18 over [40021576, 45121904] shows it holds 0x4eb611232ce3a738d9ee20467a5dd2ecf3b2d919 unchanged from creation to the incident (no NewImplementation in the window), the delegator runtime is byte-identical at both blocks, and the CToken implementation itself contains no DELEGATECALL, so the executing code dates from deployment.

disposition.reason: An admitted incident declares this discovery lead.

legacyRecord.name: Makina DUSD Caliber AUM revaluation
legacyRecord.notes: Caliber.accountForPosition() / Machine.updateTotalAum() were permissionless and valued the DUSD machine's Curve MIM-3LP3CRV position with the pool's spot calc_withdraw_one_coin(), so a ~$280M flash-loan skew of the Curve balances propagated into DUSD's share oracle and let the caller swap out of the DUSD/USDC pool at the inflated rate.

sources.ref: onchain review: Caliber 0xD1A1C248... is a BeaconProxy (beacon 0x3f5a881db86d6f495823028a1e892e7b2cd7e162, last beacon Upgraded at block 23426675, before the Caliber deployment), created 2025-10-25 by 0x6f59929ebab4502b6ccd0fffbd1436d9554050f2. Recheck (deployment basis confirmed, read from storage rather than events): the Caliber proxy's EIP-1967 beacon slot held 0x3f5a881db86d6f495823028a1e892e7b2cd7e162 unchanged over [23654997, 24273361], and the beacon's own implementation (its storage slot 1) held 0x06147e073b854521c7b778280e7d7dbafb2d4898 unchanged over the same range, both confirmed by binary-searching eth_getStorageAt; the only further address executed in the victim's context during the exploit, 0xfd162a672928bf40e5a81f0d11501d2849841fa6, is a PUSH32 constant inside that implementation. keccak(eth_getCode) on the proxy is identical at the creation and incident blocks.

legacyRecord.name: MCAI tax-wallet allowance backdoor
legacyRecord.notes: MCAI's transferFrom routed the allowance decrement through _decreaseAllowance(), which returns 0 whenever msg.sender is the token's _taxWallet, so the tax wallet could move any holder's balance with no allowance at all; it was used to pull the MCAI/WETH pair's entire MCAI reserve, sync the pair at a dust reserve and sell the tokens back for WETH.

sources.ref: onchain review: MCAI 0x810B5902CB2ac2Fa63dFE4A6935EA32aED975cc8 (verified) created 2025-01-27T23:21:35Z by 0x73478e56442b2199d95378e05fd432c98fb3a805, 4.3 hours before the drain; no EIP-1967 events. Its verified source contains `_decreaseAllowance(...) { return msg.sender != _taxWallet && (owner == _uniswapPair || spender != _deadWallet) ? amount : 0; }`, an explicit allowance bypass for the tax wallet, and the draining contract 0xdDF062714911A2e59996Eb94A57b7040Ea44309D was created by the attack-tx sender 0x0c8ecf2bbf9361fa2dd0bd29ea473fb790ab7fee, i.e. the tax wallet was attacker-controlled. Classified insider-rug rather than code-bug because the bypass is a deliberate backdoor, not a defect. 12.03 WETH at a January 2025 ETH price near $3,200 is roughly $38k. Loss converted at the incident timestamp: 12.03 WETH x $3,202.67 (DefiLlama historical ETH price) = $38,528.

disposition.reason: The legacy category insider-rug is outside the EVM code-bug cohort.

legacyRecord.name: wrsETH market priced by a faulty Chainlink RSETH/ETH feed
legacyRecord.notes: Moonwell's code worked as written: the Chainlink RSETH/ETH aggregator behind the ChainlinkCompositeOracle returned an absurd rate, so a dust deposit into the mwrsETH market was valued in the millions and Comptroller.borrowAllowed let the attacker borrow wstETH and other assets against it.

sources.ref: onchain review: victim is the mwrsETH MErc20Delegator 0xfC41B49d064Ac646015b459C522820DB9472F4B5 (creator 0x29b28b0ff5b6b26448f3ac02cd209539626d96ab, not the attacker); its comptroller 0xfBb21d0380beE3312B33c4353c8936a0F13EF26C prices it through ChainlinkOracle 0xEC942bE8A8114bFD0396A5052c36027f2cA6a9d0 -> ChainlinkCompositeOracle 0xCcC994A46c0d81c934FD6C82D89F626Aee336ADE -> RSETH/ETH feed 0xd7221b10FBBC1e1ba95Fd0B4D031C15f7F365296; distinct incident and distinct contract from the 2026-02 cbETH row in this file

re-check 2026 (deployment-basis rows with a DELEGATECALL in the runtime): CONFIRMED deployment basis. MErc20Delegator: implementation lives at storage slot 19 (slot 18 is `underlying`), held 0x1fadff493529c3fcc7ee04f1f15d19816dda45b7 continuously over a 25-point probe of [20948090, 37722882], and the only NewImplementation(address,address) event on the delegator is the 0x0 -> 0x1fadff49 write in the creation block 20948090. callTracer on the exploit tx shows the delegator delegatecalling only 0x1fadff49..., whose own runtime has no reachable DELEGATECALL.

disposition.reason: An exact adjudication excludes this lead from the primary dataset.

legacyRecord.name: Tornado Cash governance takeover via mutated proposal

sources.ref: onchain review: Governance proxy 0x5efda50f22d34f262c29268506c5fa42cb56a1ce created 2020-12-18 by 0x4e7b3769921c8dfbdb3d1b4c73558db079a180c7 (Tornado deployer), unrelated to attack sender 0x592340957ebc9e4afb0e9af221d06fdddf789de9; 2 EIP-1967 Upgraded events, the last on 2022-02-21 to implementation 0xa9689ed4a82a288e267b11ae8fe137fb4cb2177e, so the executing code was ~453 days old; the recorded tx calls execute(20) directly on the Governance proxy and emits ProposalExecuted(20); the attacker's sybil delegations were set up two days earlier from 0x092123663804f8801b9b086b03b98d706f77bd59; classified governance-design rather than code-bug because the mutated contract sat outside the victim - Governance itself behaved to spec - though a codehash pin at proposal creation (as Audius Governance has) would have blocked it

disposition.reason: An admitted incident declares this discovery lead.

legacyRecord.name: UN token price manipulation
legacyRecord.notes: The UN token sizes its internal buy-back/reward from the UN/USDT pair's live reserves, so a flash loan moved that price and let the attacker extract the pair's USDT.

sources.ref: onchain review: UN 0x1aFA48B74bA7aC0C3C5A2c8B7E24eB71D440846F created 2023-05-30T07:44:11Z by 0x797d22e9fa8f707ba061b79f278f3bdf61015d31, unrelated to attack sender 0xf84efa8a9f7e68855cf17eaac9c2f97a9d131366; no EIP-1967 Upgraded events, age measured from deployment. Loss verified onchain: 26,558.71 USDT left the UN pair 0x5F739a4AdE4341D4AEe049E679095BcCbe904Ee1 to the attacker. Boundary row: the token behaved as coded and the attacker moved the price it read.

disposition.reason: Legacy labelled this row oracle-manipulation, which names a mechanism rather than a cause. Review whether executed code violated an invariant or a persistent onchain configuration change created the vulnerable state.

legacyRecord.name: UwU Lend sUSDE oracle manipulation
legacyRecord.notes: UwU Lend's Aave-fork LendingPool priced sUSDE from an oracle reading Curve pool spot state, so a flash-loan sequence that skewed those pools inflated sUSDE collateral value and let the attacker borrow out most of the protocol's other markets.

sources.ref: onchain review: LendingPool proxy 0x2409aF0251DCB89EE3Dee572629291f9B087c668 (verified as InitializableImmutableAdminUpgradeabilityProxy) created 2022-09-19T16:55:47Z by 0x50831130c4b0aa78fca9edaa39d7339a9620d751, not the attack-tx sender 0x841ddf093f5188989fa1524e7b893de64b421f47. It emits no EIP-1967 Upgraded events, so the EIP-1967 implementation slot was read directly: 0x05bfa9157e92690b179033ca2f6dd1e86b25ea4d at the creation block, the pre-incident block 20061318 and today alike, confirming the implementation never changed and age runs from deployment (629.8 days). A second exploit on the same pool three days later (tx 0x9235e0662e230bdfa94f56f4932fd09a95fea17e4b9b44a4f40a59449e216110, ~$3.7M, src/test/2024-06/UwuLend_Second_exp.sol) is the same victim contract and root cause and is not recorded as a separate row.

deployment-basis recheck extended to the whole delegate set: callTracer shows the LendingPool proxy delegatecalling 0x05bfa9157e92690b179033ca2f6dd1e86b25ea4d (the EIP-1967 implementation) plus the Aave-style linked libraries 0x3c0ada81038a078cc1272ac22745ddd1ab8839af and 0xaede01960810a655aecf86278bfdf5c968198b89, which are link-time constants inside that implementation and cannot be repointed. The implementation slot returns 0x05bfa915... at the creation block 15568883, at the incident block 20061319 and at all 201 evenly spaced samples in between, and the proxy runtime is byte-identical at both blocks. Deployment is the correct basis; 629.8 days.

disposition.reason: An admitted incident declares this discovery lead.

legacyRecord.name: Warp Finance LP collateral valuation manipulation
legacyRecord.notes: WarpControl valued deposited Uniswap V2 LP collateral from the pair's live spot reserves, so a flash-loaned swap that doubled the WETH-DAI LP price let the attacker borrow 3.86m DAI and 3.9m USDC against collateral worth a fraction of that; the lending code itself behaved as written.

sources.ref: onchain review: resolved the victim from the attack tx logs - 0xba539b9a is the verified WarpControl (the borrow authoriser and collateral valuer); the WarpVaultSC lenders 0x6046c3ab/0xae465fd3/0xdadd9ba3 and WarpVaultLP 0x13db1cb4 also appear. Created 2020-12-16 by 0x8f3e8a974d6eb27316054147fdf0e960dab2e1b3, not by attack sender 0xebc6bd6a - only 1.7 days before the incident, matching Warp's 2020-12-09 launch. lossUsd is the borrowed 3.86m DAI + 3.9m USDC, both USD-pegged 1:1

disposition.reason: An admitted incident declares this discovery lead.

sources.ref: re-check 2026 (deployment-basis rows with a DELEGATECALL in the runtime): CONFIRMED deployment basis. The recorded victim is the implementation contract, not the proxy: in the exploit tx it is only ever reached through 30 DELEGATECALL frames from the proxy 0x40465755eb5846d655bbcc8c186a477469f9ce36. That proxy's EIP-1967 slot holds 0x9153e149... at the incident, and its Upgraded history is 0x5a02541cb59efcc23c581f8d6599fc9810e7ea50 (block 74633620, 2025-07-31T15:36:56Z), 0xfd28a6e45402a4322fed47f883b765f03327b36e (block 76558148, 2025-09-17T11:29:20Z) and 0x9153e149... (block 76904623, 2025-09-26T00:49:43Z) - the last of those is 8 s after the implementation's own deployment at 1758847775, so measuring from either address gives the same age to within 8 seconds.

onchain review: victim re-anchored from implementation 0x9153e149b0d90dea634ed9f7df6ff71c2109b654 to the proxy the protocol runs at, 0x40465755eb5846d655bbcc8c186a477469f9ce36, which holds that implementation in its EIP-1967 slot and emits the exploit transaction's logs while the implementation emits none; age measured from when the proxy started running the implementation rather than from the implementation's own deployment (16150006s -> 16149998s)

legacyRecord.name: Zoomer buyback contract spot-price manipulation
legacyRecord.notes: The unverified ZOOMER buyback contract paid ETH for ZOOMER at the Uniswap V2 spot price, so a 200 ETH flash-loaned buy that pumped the WETH/ZOOMER pair let five freshly created contracts each sell 30.27M ZOOMER into it at the inflated rate.

sources.ref: onchain review: victim 0x9700204D77A67A18eA8F1B47275897b21e5eFA97 created 2024-02-18T03:43:47Z by 0x3e49da81338d87c22f2f2c16d2874de2ad28c581, not the attack-tx sender 0xb0380b6d7a63e7cbf274c3b3c8838abbd6bd4abe; no EIP-1967 events. Balance diff across blocks 19291249->19291250 shows the victim's ETH falling from 17.300 to 0.152 ETH while its ZOOMER balance rose by 145.1M, confirming it bought ZOOMER for ETH at the manipulated spot price; ~17 ETH at a February 2024 ETH price near $2,950 clears the $1,000 floor. Repeated through five CREATE2 helper contracts, each capped at 30,265,400 ZOOMER. Loss converted at the incident timestamp: 17.15 ETH x $2,927.14 (DefiLlama historical ETH price) = $50,200.

legacyRecord.name: USD0PPSubVault deployer-key compromise and malicious upgrade
legacyRecord.notes: No contract flaw: Zoth's deployer key held the UUPS upgrade authority for the USD0PPSubVaultUpgradeable proxy, and whoever obtained it called upgradeToAndCall() to install a self-authored implementation with an unrestricted withdraw(), emptying the vault 36 seconds later.

sources.ref: onchain review: proxy 0x82f3a039...e43e was created by Zoth deployer 0x3604582f56565d7060D73829FfB9EBD579218Dca (not the attack sender 0x3b33c5Cd...); the last of its seven Upgraded events, at block 22094140 in tx 0xb2335f7bf58abbcaa006d0a2bed7db2c64a5dabed56fb1759260adc012c49abe, installed the attacker's own implementation 0xc89d7894341e13d5067d003af5346b257d861f56 — so the mechanical code age of 36s measures the attacker's implementation, not Zoth's; this row is context only and never feeds the curve

disposition.reason: An exact adjudication excludes this lead from the primary dataset.
